STEPPER MOTOR CONTROLLERS
DISCUSSION
A system which contains a step pattern and driver circuit is called a Stepper Controller.
A typical Stepper Controller must have provisions for a variety of motor characteristics.
Due to the digital characteristics of the stepper, it is ideally suited for microprocessor control.
Most stepper controllers utilize digital circuit components such as flip-flops and latches.

The simplest type of stepper controller is a full step single phase controller.
The circuit schematic is nothing more than a simple J-K shift register.
To eliminate the need to re-input data every 4th clock pulse, a feedback loop from QD to Data In can be employed.
The output signals show a sequential step pattern generated by the tracking edge clock pulses.
Notice that the shaft right circuit relates to a QA to QD coil energizing sequence, or, a CW rotation of the stepper motor output shaft.
To reverse motor direction, coils must be energized in a reverse order (QD to QA).

The FWD/REV switch will send either a logic 0 to the upper AND and a logic 1 to the lower AND gates or vice versa.
Notice that the sequence of coil winding activations can be reversed by the FWD/REV switch and the inverting amplifier.

A two phase full step generator is practically identical to a single phase generator. Clocking two windings at the same time provides smoother step operation.

Time delaying a logic 1 data input for two clock pulses generates the 2f full step pattern. You will note the step sequence is maintained but held for one clock pulse longer.
To reverse the stepper rotation direction, coil sequence must be reversed.
The input DATA and CLOCK signal frequencies must not exceed the Slew Rate and Error Free Start-Stop rates of the stepper motor.
The slew rate (SR) is the maximum number of steps that a stepper motor can use and still operate correctly.f the stepper motor.

The Error Free Start-Stop (EFSS) is a rate that is used when a stepper motor is first started or when the stepper motor is stopped. This rate is less than the slew rate and is normally between 100 and 1000 pulses per second..
The stepper motor is ramped up and down in normal operation...RPM.
A block diagram of a ramp up - ramp down circuit is illustrated below.
A digital start signal is applied to the latch input. The output latches high...
The integrator provides the ramp up signal after receiving the HIGH from the latch...
The integrator output is applied to a voltage controlled oscillator (VCO)...age controlled oscillator.
The VCO output starts low but increases in frequency with the applied voltage. This allows the stepping motor to gradually increase speed.
The shift register receives the input from the VCO and the clock input. Neither input exceeds the error free start-stop rating of the stepper motor.
The shift register then sequences the output based on the inputs...
The step signal is applied to the drivers and then the motor windings. The motor continues rotation until a stop signal is received which begins the ramp down process.
